gen_risks.description: Inadequate handling, storage, and disposal of hazardous laboratory reagents, chemicals, and healthcare waste could cause environmental contamination and community health hazards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Update and implement National Healthcare Waste Management Plans, provide laboratory biosafety training, and mandate standard waste management protocols across all supported facilities.
gen_risks.evidence: laboratories will be supplied with reagents, chemicals, and equipment that may constitute medical waste once used.

gen_risks.description: Fiduciary risks and questionable expenditures arising from decentralized project activities, local-level capacity building, workshops, and emergency procurements in remote areas.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adapt and disseminate financial management procedure manuals down to local implementation partners, customize accounting software, and mandate regular internal and external financial audits.
gen_risks.evidence: several activities under the project like workshops, trainings and the local-level capacity building are at risk to generate questionable expenditures

gen_risks.description: Fiscal constraints, declining oil revenues, and low domestic health budget allocations in participating countries threaten the long-term financial sustainability of health security investments.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide technical assistance to integrate health security into Medium-Term Expenditure Frameworks, establish budget coding, and promote domestic resource mobilization and public-private partnerships.
gen_risks.evidence: low government funding... led to a high reliance on household's out-of-pocket payments

gen_risks.description: Delays in recruiting key PIU specialists (auditors, environmental, social, and GBV experts) and customizing accounting software within mandated legal covenant deadlines post-effectiveness.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize Project Preparation Advances (PPAs), fast-track recruitment procedures, and leverage qualified specialists from existing World Bank project implementation units.
gen_risks.evidence: Recruit an external auditor... recruit an internal auditor... customize existing accounting software no later than three to six months after Effective Date.

gen_risks.description: Delays in executing mandatory institutional agreements (such as CEMAC's MoU with WOAH within 90 days and WAHO collaboration within 30 days) delaying regional activity implementation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Initiate MoU drafting and inter-agency consultations during early project preparation, with close progress tracking by the Regional Coordination Committee.
gen_risks.evidence: enter into a Memorandum of Understanding (the 'MoU') with the WOAH... no later than ninety (90) days after the Effective Date

gen_risks.description: Exclusion of vulnerable or disadvantaged populations (IDPs, refugees, indigenous groups, rural women, and mobile populations) from emergency healthcare and health communication.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement country-specific Stakeholder Engagement Plans, Indigenous Peoples Plans, and tailored, inclusive Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE) strategies.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential social risks... relate to: (ii) the exclusion of vulnerable or disadvantaged groups

gen_risks.description: Substantial risk of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH) associated with civil works labor influx and community deployment of health/community workers.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and implement country-specific SEA/SH Action Plans within two months of effectiveness, recruit dedicated GBV specialists, enforce worker codes of conduct, and establish GBV-sensitive GRMs.
gen_risks.evidence: The overall project SEA/SH risks are judged to be substantial... increased presence of new health workforce... may create concerns

gen_risks.description: Active armed conflict, FCV conditions, and political instability (e.g., Boko Haram attacks, regional unrest) obstructing project execution and access in fragile zones.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare Security Risk Assessments and Security Management Plans, apply flexible procurement arrangements in FCV areas, and utilize third-party monitoring where direct access is constrained.
gen_risks.evidence: Fragility in AFW is exacerbated by conflict and violence... Boko Haram attacks in Cameroon and ongoing unrest in CAR

gen_risks.description: Regulatory bottlenecks and lack of cross-border agreements impeding real-time epidemiological data sharing, biological specimen transport, and synchronized regional outbreak responses.
gen_risks.mitigation: Finance CEMAC to facilitate harmonized regional health security policies, establish standardized biological specimen transportation protocols, and execute formal cross-border data-sharing agreements.
gen_risks.evidence: Regional signed agreements for cross-border information sharing on health security guided by the One Health principles.

gen_risks.description: Severe climate shocks such as flooding and extreme heat damaging health/laboratory infrastructure and triggering outbreaks of climate-sensitive vector- and waterborne diseases.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate green and resilient infrastructure design standards (EDGE certification), install solar backup power in laboratories, and integrate climate shock alerts into surveillance systems.
gen_risks.evidence: More frequent flooding events in CAR and Chad drive recurrent cholera outbreaks... climate-sensitive disease risks

gen_risks.description: Environmental degradation, occupational hazards, and community nuisances (dust, noise, construction waste) resulting from the construction and rehabilitation of laboratories and health facilities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare site-specific Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs) prior to civil works, enforce contractor safety standards, and implement proper waste disposal guidelines.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential risks and impacts can include: (ii) disposal and management of building/construction wastes; (iii) occupational health and safety risks

gen_risks.description: Weak institutional capacity and inter-ministerial coordination constraints across human, animal, and environmental health sectors impeding operationalization of the One Health approach.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish multi-sectoral National Steering Committees, provide fiduciary and operational coaching to PIU staff, and resource dedicated One Health coordination platforms.
gen_risks.evidence: gaps are primarily due to... weak institutional capacities and governance mechanisms, and insufficient multisectoral coordination

gen_risks.description: Gender disparities restricting female health professionals' access to formal advanced technical training programs (FETP/FELTP, ISAVET) and technical decision-making positions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement targeted outreach and gender quotas to encourage female recruitment into field epidemiology and veterinary training, utilizing flexible training formats.
gen_risks.evidence: women remain underrepresented in formal epidemiological training and decision-making

gen_risks.description: Large cross-border influxes of refugees and internally displaced persons straining border health posts and local health service capacity during infectious disease outbreaks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen point-of-entry (PoE) disease surveillance, establish cross-border emergency response mechanisms, and allocate health service delivery resources to refugee and host community facilities.
gen_risks.evidence: Chad currently hosts over 1.5 million IDPs and refugees... Porous borders, migration... heighten cross-border health threats

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk (Moderate), considering fragility, socio-political instability, violence and weak governance of beneficiary countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close engagement by the World Bank to coordinate activities with other key partners.

gt_risks.description: Technical design risk (Substantial), considering the complexities of coordinating national-level and regional-level activities to align and build on each other, and the different levels of readiness at country-level.
gt_risks.mitigation: Exploring the possibility of a coordinated implementation arrangement with CEMAC as the lead technical coordination body for regional activities.

gt_risks.description: Weak institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability (Substantial), combined with overstretched or nonexistent PIUs in respective countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Strengthening the existing PIUs and intensive capacity building and targeted TA for newly established PIUs.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk (Substantial) due to weak governance structures and inadequate FM systems.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on fiduciary processes.

gt_risks.description: E&S risk (Substantial) given the security risks associated with service delivery in FCV (fragility, conflict, and violence) settings.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on managing E&S risks.
